{"source": "Oriki (scraped)", "genre": "praise_poetry", "language": "yoruba", "praise_text": "Iseyin Oro, Omo Ebedi moko,
Ni bi ti ewe nje ariyeke,
Ti popo o nje belewo,
Ti igi nje oluwanran,
Ti agbado ojo nje t' opabodi.
Ilu ma gba fere,
Kii b' alejo nibi t' o tiwa,
Osalasala ti f' owo alejo bomi,
Eyin gbo gambari, E gbo sokoto,
E gbo 'Lorin, E gbo Oyo,
E gbo 'Badan,
Sugbon e ko gbo,
Ohun ti ilu Mokin nwi
Bi e ba se gege ote,
K' amu t'aseyin kuro,
B'o ba d'ojo ere,
Ke ran ni s'ebedi moko
Eni ba nfe aso 'tata ti ile Yoruba,
eni ki won kori si Iseyin,

{"source": "Oriki (scraped)", "genre": "praise_poetry", "language": "yoruba", "praise_text": "Osogbo Oroki Asala
Osogbo ilu Aro, Aro dede bi Okun
Are Op'eta, Are p'eta a gba
Osogbo Oroki gbe Onile o tun gbe Ajeji
Osogbo Oroki Omo yeye Osun
Yeye Atewogbeja Aniyun Labebe
Eleyele Aro, Olode Ega, Ega susu ni yara
Ewure Orangun ti n je lese Gbagede
Lese Gbagede ni ti ije
Aguntan Orangun nii je lese Yara
Akuko gagara t'o rori Ope ree le tente
Nibe ni won ti n pe Alara tantan
Ogboju Obinrin tii fi owo gbogboro yo omo re lofin
Yeye Larooye t'o ti Ipole di onile losogbo
Yeye Timehin akikanju Ode t'o m'erin wa mo ilu Osogbo,
Osogbo Oroki omo Olofin agba Ife
Omo Owa Oluyeye, Omo Obokun
Omo odo kan odo kan ti won n pe losun
Omo atenigbola olodo ide
Ogun kan, Ogun kan ti won n ja loroki ile
Obinrin gbona, Okunrin ko gbodo koja
Bi Okorokoro ti n gba oko niju
Bee ni Ogbaagbaa n run bala bi ose
Opo gbegiri l'osun fi segun Fulani
Ogun ko gbogbo jami, mo gbekeleOsun
Oroki tii ba Eja nla soro, tii ran iko ni'se
Osun Osogbo rere ni'Osun funmi
Ire Owo, Ire Omo, Ire Aiku Baale Oro
Osun t'ori ajigbara, leke o bawon ni orun gigun
O'tori ide wewe o bawon lapa gbogboro
B'oba wu agba Ijesha a san'so si bebere idi
B'oba wu Morokahan a san'so Gbogbo lo itan
Osogbo Oroki t'oni lakokan l'o ni Ohuntofo
Oun loni Ogidan tii fi Odo ide fo'gun
Omo atupa merindinlogun tii tan loroki ile
B'oba tan f'oba a tan f'osun
A tun tan fun irunmole a tan f'eniyan
Osogbo wumi ide ki n lo d'agbala osun
Ni bi ti won ti n re ro ti won tun ti n gundo ide,
A kii b'omi s'ote, a kii b'omi s'ota
Omi l'a buwe, omi la bu mu
Ore yeye Osun Osogbo o.", "meaning": "", "category": "town", "subject_type": "town", "origin": "YorubaLibrary — https://www.yorubalibrary.com/culture/oriki_yoruba/oriki_for_towns/oriki_ilu_osogbo.html", "source_url": "https://www.yorubalibrary.com/culture/oriki_yoruba/oriki_for_towns/oriki_ilu_osogbo.html", "license": "scraped, no explicit licence — research use, attributed", "dialect_assigned_default": false}

{"source": "Oriki (scraped)", "genre": "praise_poetry", "language": "yoruba", "praise_text": "Ife Ooye Lagbo
Omo Olodo Kan Oteere
Omo Olodo Kan Otaara
Odo To San Wereke,To San Wereke
To Dehinkunle Oshinle To Dabata
To Dehinkunle Adelawe To Dokun
Onikee Ko Gbodo Bu Mu
Ababaja Won Ko Gbodo Buwe
Ogedegede Onisoboro Ni Yio Mu Omi Do Naa Gbe
Soboro Mi Wumi, Eje Ki Ibi Dandan Maa Ba Alabe
Won Kii Duro Ki Wa Nife Ooni, Won Kii Bere Ki Wa Nife Ooye
Ko Ga, Ko Bere Laa Ki Wa Nife Oodaye
Bi Won Ko Si Ki Wa Nife, Won Kii To Abere
Oju Bintin La Fi N Wo Ni
Emi Wa Ki Oba Nife, Mo Lo Akun
Oba Nii Lo Sese Efun
Adimula, Won A Ni Apalado
Bante Gbooro, Ni Mufe Wumi
Segi Owo Ati Tese,
Kafari Apakan Ka Dapakan Si
Yeepa Orisa, Aso Funfun
Oun Nii Mu Ile Olufe Wumi
Apadari Eni, Apalado Eniyan
Ebo Ojoojumo, Nii Mu Ile Won Su Nii Lo
Awa Lomo Oni Fitila Rebete
Ina Ko Nii Ku Nibe Tosan Toru
Ibe Ni Baba Wa Gbe N Ka Owo Eyo
Awa Lomo Onilu Kan, Ilu Kan
Ti Won N Fawo Ekun Se
Aketepe Eti Erin Ni Won Fi Nse Osan Re
Onikeke Ko Gbodo Jo
Ababaja Ko Gbodo Yese
Kikida Onisoboro Ni Yio Jo Ilu Naa Ya
Ogun Ko See Da Gbe
Baba Taani Ko Mo Wipe Irin Ti Po Lagbede
Oun Ti O Ba Mu Alagbede,
Ko Ni Mu Eni To N Fin Ina", "meaning": "Ife, land of Oòyè,
Child of Olódòkan Òtẹ̀rẹ̀,
Child of Olódòkan Òtáàrà,
River that flows with winding bends,
That flows and reaches the courtyard of Òṣinlẹ̀,
Flows and reaches the courtyard of Adélawẹ̀,
That flows and reaches the dwelling of Òníkẹ́ẹ̀.
No one must break the sacred calabash,
No one must split the sacred gourd.
It is the Onísoboro who draws water,
Soboro water refreshes me.
Let hardship not befall the people of Àlàbẹ̀.
They do not stand without loving the Ọọ̀ni,
They do not begin without loving Oòyè.
Oòyè is lofty, yet still beloved.
Even if they are absent, love for Oòyè remains.
They do not thread the needle with half an eye,
It is with full sight they behold me.
I salute the King of Ife.
I go with the royal chalk, and with the sacred white powder of Àdìmúlà.
They say: "Apàlàdò, broad and mighty,"
In Ife I drink from the beaded cup,
With bracelets of hand and foot.
Half is woven, half is tied,
Dedicated to the multitude of Òrìṣà.
White cloth adorns the land of lovers,
It refreshes the leader of men.
Daily sacrifices sustain the land,
We are children of the lamp,
The flame never dies there, day or night.
There our fathers lived,
Counting cowries in abundance.
We are children of the drummers,
The single drum that makes the leopard dance.
The elephant's ear is the mat they spread at noon.
The Oníkẹ́kẹ́ must not break the calabash,
Must not scatter the sacred beads.
It is the Onísoboro who beats the drum,
The war cannot be undone.
Father Tààní knows that iron is plentiful,
And that whoever seizes the blacksmith's iron,
Cannot seize the one who kindles the fire.", "category": "town", "subject_type": "town", "origin": "HabaNaija — https://www.habanaija.com/oriki-ile-ife/", "source_url": "https://www.habanaija.com/oriki-ile-ife/", "license": "scraped, no explicit licence — research use, attributed", "dialect_assigned_default": false}

{"source": "Oriki (scraped)", "genre": "praise_poetry", "language": "yoruba", "praise_text": "Iree Oye, Iree Alalubosa
Oro Iree Kii Rin Are Lo Nsa
Iree Oye, Itake Ola
Ikomi Oge Omo Oyeniran
Ikomi Oge Omo Laro, Omo Arolu,
Omo Oyekun, Omo Akoiisa
Ta Lo So Pe Onipee Ko Lomi
Ta Lo So Pe Onipee Ko Lodo
Afelele Lomi, Aro Pekun Ni Pee
Aro Pekun Lomi Ayaba Ni Pee
Ta Lo So Pe Aree Ko Lomi
Ta Lo So Pe Aree Ko Lodo
Akeepa Lomi Isun, Yoko Lomi Amu
N Ho Lo Ile Ma Lo Bu Abo Mu
Ma Bu Odo Oke San Ese
Ara Jobaji, Agbara Nlelegbo N We
Ti Won Ba We Asa, Asa A Sa Won Lojugun.
Yoko Ngbe Komi Oge Bo Wa Isale
Ailu Semi Komi Oge Ma Je Nba
Alagba Lugbo Mi Lo.
Ikomi Oge, Ara Jobaji, Ara Ilegudu,
Ilegudu Ayabu Ero,
Ara Ori Oke, Ara Ori Ipoole
Omo Efon To Ro Iwo Ide
Komi Oge, Ara Ope Aanu
Jobaji, Omo Omi Kikun Ti Nta Si Ayaba Laso,
Komi Oge Ti N We Lodo Ti Gbogbo
Omoge Nyo Owo Ose Ti Won So
Wipe Bi Eleyi Ko Ba Je Oko Eni
Asi Je Ale Eni
Komi Oge, Omo Oyeniran,
Komi Oge Lomo Onirinwo Adie
Ti Gbogbo Won Ngbe Kekeke Lori Eyin,
Eyin Lomo Obinrin Jowu Ore Re
Ti O Nba Ewu Jowu Loko
Komi Igbati O Mo Wipe O Ma Jowu
Ki Lo Mu Mi Wa Se Loko;
Ara Jobaji Mo Gbele Huwo
Komi Oge Mo Gbele Hu Segi,
Mo Kakuro Iyun Niran,
Mo Gbele Hu Segi, Segi Mi Dudu Janjan.
Komi Oge, Omo Abowo Sirimusirimu,
Komi Lomo Okunkun Sirimusirimu
Okunkun Lowon, Owo Mi Ko Won
Ni Igbo Nla, Ara Ori Oke,
Ara Ori Ipole, Ara Ope Aanu.
Komi Oge Omo Ari Igba Nla Bu Owo Fun Ayaba!
Ara Jobaji, Ti Mo Ba Ki Yin Titi
Ti Mo Ba Sin Yin Titi N Ho Pada
Legudu, Eyin Lomo Ajoji Ki Ba
Won Degbo Okuja, Ajoji To Ba
Wo Igbo Okuja O Deran Ebo Ni Iree
Oye Nile Omi Ru De!
Komi Oge Omo Onipe", "meaning": "Iree Oye, Iree of onions and wealth,
That never walks in vain.
Iree Oye, source of honor,
Child of Oyeniran, descendant of Laro,
Offspring of Arolu, child of Oyekun,
Descendant of Akoiisa.
Who says the spring has no water?
Who says the spring has no river?
The spring flows abundantly,
The stream never ceases.
Who says the queen has no water?
Who says the queen has no river?
The queen's stream flows endlessly.
The fountain flows, the stream gushes,
The calabash floats downstream,
While the clay pot drifts to the riverbank.
The power of Jobaji,
The strength of Nlelegbo,
When they wash with tradition,
Tradition protects them for generations.
The calabash carries honor downstream,
The lineage of Oyeniran endures.
Descendants of Jobaji, of Ilegudu,
Of the mountain top, of Ipoole,
Children of Efon who wear brass ornaments.
Descendants of flowing water,
Whose daughters are adorned in fine cloth,
Whose maidens wash at the river,
And whose beauty makes men desire them.
Komi Oge, child of Oyeniran,
Child of countless hens,
Whose eggs are carried gently.
Women envy their peers,
Yet now they must share husbands.
Jobaji's descendants,
I adorn myself with coral,
I wear black beads shining brightly.
Komi Oge, child of mystery,
Dark and radiant,
My hands reach into the great forest,
From the mountain top, from Ipoole,
From the grove of mercy.
Komi Oge, child of abundance,
Who gives wealth to the queen.
Jobaji's descendants,
If I praise you endlessly,
I will return to Ilegudu.
Foreigners who enter the forest of Okuja,
Will meet sacrifices at Iree Oye,
Land of flowing waters!", "category": "town", "subject_type": "town", "origin": "HabaNaija — https://www.habanaija.com/oriki-iree-traditional-yoruba-praise-poetry/", "source_url": "https://www.habanaija.com/oriki-iree-traditional-yoruba-praise-poetry/", "license": "scraped, no explicit licence — research use, attributed", "dialect_assigned_default": false}

{"source": "Oriki (scraped)", "genre": "praise_poetry", "language": "yoruba", "praise_text": "Ijebu omo alare,
omo awujale,
omo arojo joye,
omo'alagemo ogun woyowoyo,
Omo aladiye ogogomoga,
omo adiye balokun omilili,
ara orokun, ara o radiye,
omo ohun seni oyoyonyo,
oyoyo mayomo ohun seni olepani,
omo dudu ile komobe se njosi,
pupa tomo be se okuku sinle,
omo moreye mamaroko,
morokotan eye matilo,
omo moni isunle mamalobe,
obe tin benile komoile baba tobiwan lomo,
Omo onigbo ma'de,
omo'onigbo mawo mawo,
omo onigbo ajoji magbodowo,
ajoji tobawo gboro yio di ebora ile baba tobi wan lomo.
Ijebu omo ere niwa,
omo olowo isembaye,
towo kuji to dode, koto dowo eru,
koto dowo omo.
Orisa jendabi onile yi,
niwan finpe igba ijebu owo,
kelebe ijebu owo, ito ijebu owo,
dudu ijebu owo, pupa ijebu owo,
kekere ijebu owo, agba ijebu owo.
Ijebu ode ijebu ni,
ijebu igbo ijebu ni, ijebu isara ijebu ni,
ayepe ijebu, ikorodu ijebu ijebu noni,
Ijebu Omo Oni Ile nla,
Ijebu Omo Alaso nla!
Ajuwaase ooo", "meaning": "Child of Ijebu, descendant of Alare,
Child of the Awujale (the king of Ijebu),
Child of one who deliberates before taking a title,
Child of the keeper of the sacred Agemo festival, with its countless masquerades.
Child of the owner of countless hens, and of the hen that lays eggs by the seashore,
Native of Orokun, native of Oradiye.
Child of one whose possessions are plentiful,
Whose wealth brings joy,
Child of one whose riches cannot be hidden.
Child of the black soil where the hoe strikes and food grows,
Child of the red earth where the rooster scratches the ground.
Child of one who owns many birds,
Whose birds never wander away,
Child of one who owns abundant soup,
Soup so plentiful it fills the house,
Child of the great father whose children are many.
Child of the forest owner who wears the crown, the forest owner who commands respect, and child of the forest owner who forbids strangers from cutting wood,
For if strangers cut wood carelessly,
The land of the great father will rise in wrath.
Ijebu, child of playfulness and merriment,
Child of wealth that never diminishes,
Whose money flows like a river,
Enough to buy slaves, enough to raise children.
The deity Jendabi is the guardian of this land,
To whom the people dedicate their offerings:
Cowries of Ijebu wealth, small cowries of Ijebu wealth,
White cowries of Ijebu wealth, Black cowries of Ijebu wealth,
Red cowries of Ijebu wealth, Little cowries of Ijebu wealth, Great cowries of Ijebu wealth.
Ijebu of the town, Ijebu of the forest, Isara, Ayepe, Ikorodu, all are Ijebu.
Ijebu, child of the great house, and child of the great cloth!
Ajuwaase ooo! (A blessing chant, meaning "May it be fulfilled!")", "category": "town", "subject_type": "town", "origin": "HabaNaija — https://www.habanaija.com/oriki-ijebu-meaning-history-praise-poetry/", "source_url": "https://www.habanaija.com/oriki-ijebu-meaning-history-praise-poetry/", "license": "scraped, no explicit licence — research use, attributed", "dialect_assigned_default": false}

{"source": "Oriki (scraped)", "genre": "praise_poetry", "language": "yoruba", "praise_text": "Oyo omo Alaafin

Ase k'o le baa di'ja
Ko le baa di aapon
K'omo oba le ri je nibe
Oyo l'o gbin agbado oran
S'ehinkule elehinkule
Elehinkule ko gbodo yaa je
Beeni ko si gbodo tu u danu
Omo iku ti'ku ko le pa, Omo arun t'arun ko le gbe de
Omo ofo, t'ofo ko le se", "meaning": "Oyo, child of Alaafin Ojo who played sekere in the marketplace, child of Atiba.
He tells the wealthy to spend their wealth,
He tells the bonded servant to cast off slavery.
So that battles may be fought, contests may be joined,
So that the prince may find sustenance there.
Oyo is the one who plants maize of destiny,
Behind every household,
No household must neglect it,
Nor must it be discarded carelessly.
Child of death whom death cannot kill, of sickness whom sickness cannot overcome,
Child of loss whom loss cannot destroy.", "category": "town", "subject_type": "town", "origin": "HabaNaija — https://www.habanaija.com/oriki-oyo/", "source_url": "https://www.habanaija.com/oriki-oyo/", "license": "scraped, no explicit licence — research use, attributed", "dialect_assigned_default": false}
